appendix_basis: Appendix J(c)(1), Example (i): Monthly payments (regular first period).  ([Federal Reserve][1])

inputs.payment_schedule: 24 monthly payments of $230; advance 1-10-78; first payment 2-10-78

unit_period_analysis: The common period is 1 month, so the unit-period is 1 month and w = 12 unit-periods per year. From 1-10-78 to 2-10-78 is exactly 1 unit-period, so t = 1 and f = 0. ([Federal Reserve][1])
computation: Appendix J uses A = [P × ä̈_24] / [(1 + fi)(1+i)^t]. With f = 0 and t = 1: 5000 = [230 × ä̈_24] / (1+i), where ä̈_24 = 1 + 1/(1+i) + ... + 1/(1+i)^23. Equivalently, 5000 = 230 × [1/(1+i) + 1/(1+i)^2 + ... + 1/(1+i)^24]. Solving iteratively gives i ≈ 0.008071423385 per month. Annual APR = 12 × 0.008071423385 × 100 = 9.68570806%, which rounds to 9.69%. ([Federal Reserve][1])
weakest_point: The published example states 9.69%; the exact iteration sequence used by the historical calculator is not reproduced in the HTML, although the actuarial equation reproduces the result.

appendix_basis: Appendix J(c)(1), Example (ii): Monthly payments (long first period). ([Federal Reserve][1])

inputs.payment_schedule: 36 monthly payments of $200; advance 2-10-78; first payment 4-1-78

unit_period_analysis: The unit-period is 1 month and w = 12. From 3-1-78 through 4-1-78 is 1 full unit-period, giving t = 1. From 2-10-78 through 3-1-78 is 19 days, so f = 19/30. Appendix J treats the fractional-period rate as f × i. ([Federal Reserve][1])
weakest_point: The distinctive Appendix J treatment is the 19/30 fractional month applied through the factor (1 + (19/30)i), rather than using a generic day-count exponent.

appendix_basis: Appendix J(c)(5), Example (i): Single-advance, single-payment, term less than one year measured in days. ([Federal Reserve][1])
unit_period_analysis: The term is 255 days, less than one year and not a whole number of months. Appendix J therefore makes the unit-period the term itself: 1 unit-period = 255 days, with w = 365/255. The entire term is one unit-period, so t = 1 and f = 0. ([Federal Reserve][1])
computation: Appendix J Form 1 gives I = 100w(P/A − 1). Substitute w = 365/255, P = 1080, A = 1000: I = 100 × (365/255) × (1080/1000 − 1) = 100 × (365/255) × 0.08 = 11.45098039%. Rounded to two decimals, APR = 11.45%. The equivalent Form 4 equation is 1000 = 1080/[(1+0i)(1+i)^1], giving i = 1080/1000 − 1 = 0.08; multiplying by 365/255 gives the same APR. ([Federal Reserve][1])
weakest_point: The important Appendix J-specific point is that the 255-day term becomes one unit-period and the annualization factor is 365/255.

case_name: Monthly payments with irregular first and final payments
appendix_basis: Appendix J(c)(4), Example (i): Monthly payments (regular first period, irregular first payment, and irregular final payment). ([Federal Reserve][1])

inputs.payment_schedule: First payment $250; 22 regular payments of $230; final payment $280; 24 total payments; advance 1-10-78; first payment 2-10-78

unit_period_analysis: The unit-period is 1 month and w = 12. The first payment is exactly one month after the advance, so t = 1 and f = 0. There are 24 payments total: the first is $250, payments 2 through 23 are $230, and payment 24 is $280. ([Federal Reserve][1])
weakest_point: The intermediate regular-payment series is reconstructed from the published special equation; the published result itself is 10.90%.

case_name: Mortgage with varying payments and irregular first period
appendix_basis: Appendix J(c)(6), Table 3: Mortgage with varying payments. ([Federal Reserve][1])

inputs.payment_schedule: Monthly payments varying from $291.81 in year 1 through $369.50 in year 30; first payment 6-1-78 and subsequent payments monthly through the 30-year schedule; advance 4-10-78
inputs.finance_charge_or_payment_amounts: First payment $291.81; second payment $300.18; third $308.78; continuing as the published 360-payment schedule, ending with $369.50

unit_period_analysis: The unit-period is 1 month and w = 12. From 5-1-78 through 6-1-78 is 1 full month, so t = 1. From 4-10-78 through 5-1-78 is 21 days, giving f = 21/30. ([Federal Reserve][1])
computation: Appendix J gives the exact special-form equation: 39688.56 = ä̈_12 / [(1+(21/30)i)(1+i)] × [291.81 + 300.18/(1+i)^12 + 308.78/(1+i)^24 + ... + 369.50/(1+i)^348]. Solve this equation iteratively for the monthly unit-period rate i. The solution is i ≈ 0.008166666667. Annual APR = 12 × 0.008166666667 × 100 = 9.80%, rounded to two decimals. ([Federal Reserve][1])
weakest_point: The published equation compresses the complete 360-payment schedule with an ellipsis; the complete intervening payment amounts are not all reproduced here, so the displayed abbreviated equation cannot independently be mechanically recomputed without the full Table 3 schedule.
